Linear Algebra

Load DoubleFloats and LinearAlgebra for factorizations and matrix operations. Use Julia's usual array syntax with an explicit element type, such as Double64[2 1; 1 3] for a matrix or Double64[1, 2] for a vector.

Solve a system

using DoubleFloats, LinearAlgebra

A = Double64[2 1; 1 3]
b = Double64[1, 2]
x = A \ b
@assert norm(A * x - b, Inf) < df64"1e-30"
string.(x)
2-element Vector{String}:
 "0.19999999999999999999999999999999938"
 "0.60000000000000000000000000000000123"

For several right-hand sides, reuse a factorization such as F = lu(A) and solve each system with F \ b.

Operations and factorizations

TaskRepresentative functions
Inspect structureisdiag, istriu, istril, issymmetric, ishermitian, isposdef
Measure a matrixrank, cond, opnorm, det, logdet, logabsdet, tr
Work with diagonals and transposesdiag, diagind, transpose, adjoint
Solve with A \ b, invert, or find a null spaceinv, pinv, nullspace
General factorizationslu, qr, lq, svd
Square matrix factorizationseigen, schur, hessenberg
Structured factorizationscholesky for positive-definite input, bunchkaufman for symmetric or Hermitian input

eigen gives real eigenvalues and orthonormal eigenvectors for symmetric or Hermitian input. For real input with an all-real spectrum, it gives a real factorization. The default ordering sorts by real part and then imaginary part.

Use sylvester(A, B, C) for AX + XB + C = 0 and lyap(A, C) for AX + XA' + C = 0. See the Technical Guide for the implementation and dependencies of the factorizations and equation solvers.

Functions of whole matrices

For a square matrix, exp(A) is a matrix function. Use exp.(A) for an elementwise operation. The same convention applies to sqrt, log, and the trigonometric functions.

Apply functions to a triangular matrix

The matrix below is a Jordan block. It has a repeated eigenvalue and only one independent eigenvector, so it is defective. Writing it as A = I + N with N^2 = 0 gives exact formulas for the three matrix functions. The checks use those formulas at Double64 precision.

using DoubleFloats, LinearAlgebra

A = Double64[1 1; 0 1]
N = A - I
tol = df64"1e-29"

E = exp(A)
L = log(A)
R = sqrt(A)

@assert opnorm(E - exp(one(Double64)) * A, 1) < tol
@assert opnorm(L - N, 1) < tol
@assert opnorm(R - (N / 2 + I), 1) < tol
@assert iszero(E[2, 1]) && exp.(A)[2, 1] == one(Double64)

println("Checked exp, log, and sqrt on a defective triangular matrix")
Checked exp, log, and sqrt on a defective triangular matrix

Supported domains and branches

Dedicated matrix algorithms accept defective square inputs within the function's domain.

  • exp, expm1, log, log1p, log2, log10, and sqrt
  • Fractional powers A^p for supported floating-point exponents
  • sin, cos, sincos, tan, cot, DoubleFloats.csc, and DoubleFloats.sec
  • sinh, cosh, tanh, csch, sech, and coth

For real input, exp returns a real matrix. sqrt, log, and fractional powers can return complex matrices, for example when real eigenvalues are negative. A singular matrix logarithm throws SingularException. Fractional powers generally use exp(p * log(A)), so the logarithm's domain matters there too. Matrix expm1 and log1p are computed as exp(A) - I and log(A + I). Use the dotted forms if you need the corresponding scalar algorithms applied to entries.

cbrt, sinpi, cospi, and the inverse circular and hyperbolic families use matrixfunction(f, A). This helper applies f to the eigenvalues and transforms back using the eigenvectors. It requires a square, diagonalizable matrix. Here the conditioning of the eigenvector basis also affects accuracy.

Structured inputs and performance

Dense storage with exact triangular structure can take specialized routes. Triangular sqrt and log can skip Schur factorization. Eligible larger triangles also use packed products for exponentials and the circular and hyperbolic families. Eligible real diagonals use direct scalar diagonal evaluations. See the Technical Guide for the ranges, the exact half-power shortcut, and measured crossovers.
